distinguishing_features: Modifies gate-drive phase timing to shape high-frequency current distribution in DC-link capacitors
Uses phase-shifted redundant gate driving to create virtual low-impedance path via constructive interference

Decouples high-frequency ripple loop from capacitor self-inductance using control-level intervention
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce localized heating in DC-link film capacitors caused by high-frequency ripple currents without modifying passive hardware layout or adding components
parsed.viable_reason: The physics of magnetic flux cancellation via phase-shifted currents in parallel paths is well-established and applicable at typical power electronics frequencies and scales.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Shifting from passive impedance reduction to active control of current injection timing for thermal hotspot mitigation represents a non-trivial departure from conventional design practices in power electronics.
